# Results -- Study 120 (Excess-CAPE-Yield)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Shiller S&P 500 monthly
dataset, staged at `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet` (read-only; never re-fetched). The
regression sample runs 1882--2013 (the last 120 months of the file cannot have a
forward 10-year return and are excluded). As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Span (file) | Regression sample | n monthly | n non-overlapping 10yr |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|
| `shiller_sp500.parquet` | 1871-01 .. 2026-05 | 1882 .. 2013 | 1,578 | 14 |

| Series | Fingerprint |
|---|---|
| ECY (`ecy`) | `ef731d6411ab` |
| Fwd 10yr excess return (`fwd10_excess`) | `ae90dd76ee39` |

**ECY construction** (Shiller's definition):
- Earnings yield = 1 / CAPE (= 1 / PE10)
- Real bond yield = nominal 10-year long rate / 100 − trailing 12-month CPI inflation
- ECY = earnings yield − real bond yield

**Forward excess return** = annualised 10-year real equity total return (real price
appreciation + reinvested real dividends) minus the real bond yield at the *start* of the
holding period.

## Inference caveat: overlapping returns

Monthly observations overlap 120-fold for 10-year returns. The effective independent
sample size is ~14 non-overlapping windows. **All headline t-statistics and R² values in
the Signal verdict are on non-overlapping windows**; the monthly figures are shown as
context only. Using OLS on overlapping windows with even 120-lag Newey-West produces
wildly inflated t-stats (>1,000) due to the Valkanov (2003) size distortion; the correct
analysis is on non-overlapping sub-samples or Hodrick (1992) reverse regression.

## In-sample regression: ECY as a predictor of 10yr forward excess return

| Statistic | Value | Note |
|---|--:|---|
| R² (monthly, all overlapping) | **0.720** | context only; inflated by overlap |
| Correlation (monthly) | **0.849** | same caveat |
| R² (non-overlapping 10yr windows, n=14) | **0.698** | inference bar |
| Slope (non-overlapping) | **1.281** | close to 1:1 — ECY unit maps to excess return |
| OLS t-stat (non-overlapping) | **5.27** | |t| >> 2; REAL |

ECY explains ~70% of the cross-period variation in 10-year real excess returns on
non-overlapping windows — a relationship Shiller has documented since the 1990s and
confirmed repeatedly since.

## Comparison: 1/CAPE alone vs ECY

A key claim of ECY over plain CAPE: the bond-yield subtraction materially improves the
forecast because it controls for the time-varying risk-free hurdle.

| Predictor | R² (monthly) | R² (non-overlap) | t-stat (non-overlap) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **ECY = 1/CAPE − real bond yield** | 0.720 | **0.698** | **5.27** |
| 1/CAPE alone (earnings yield) | 0.184 | 0.006 | −0.27 |

The difference is stark: on non-overlapping windows, the plain earnings yield alone has
essentially zero predictive power for *excess* returns (R² = 0.006, t = −0.27), while ECY
has R² = 0.698 and a strong t. This makes economic sense: what matters for excess returns
is not the absolute earnings yield but how it compares to the current risk-free rate.

## Out-of-sample performance (50/50 split on non-overlapping windows)

First 7 non-overlapping windows (1882--1942) used to fit; last 7 (1952--2012) held out.

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| OOS R² vs historical-mean benchmark | **+0.419** |
| Train n | 7 |
| Test n | 7 |

An OOS R² of +0.42 means the ECY regression beats the naïve "always predict the
historical mean excess return" rule by 42% of the reducible error. This is a genuine
out-of-sample result, not cherry-picked. Power is low (n=7 test windows).

## 1-year horizon: the horizon effect

| Predictor | R² (monthly, 1yr fwd excess) |
|---|--:|
| ECY | 0.048 |

At the 1-year horizon, ECY explains less than 5% of forward excess return variation.
The 10-year horizon is where the signal lives; 1-year returns are too noisy for ECY to be
actionable. This is the "tide table, not stopwatch" caveat.

## ECY level distribution

| Metric | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean ECY | 5.04% |
| Std ECY | 6.62% |
| Fraction of months ECY > 0 | 85.0% |
| Mean fwd10_excess when ECY > 0 | +6.30%/yr |
| Mean fwd10_excess when ECY <= 0 | −5.02%/yr |

When ECY is negative (equity expected return below real bond yield), realised 10-year real
excess returns averaged −5%/yr. When positive, +6.3%/yr. The directional split is stark.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- REAL.** ECY clears the inference bar: R² = 0.698 on non-overlapping 10-year
  windows, OLS t = 5.27, OOS R² = +0.42. Plain 1/CAPE does not (t = −0.27 on the same
  sample). The bond-yield adjustment is load-bearing.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The signal requires a 10-year holding period. It cannot be
  expressed as a trading strategy — there is no short-term entry/exit rule, no stop, no
  capacity estimate to do. The ECY is a *valuation thermometer*, not a clock. A long-only
  investor can set long-run return expectations from ECY; they cannot time the market.
- **Forecaster vs timer? -- CONFIRMED.** ECY is a long-horizon return forecaster
  (confirmed REAL), not a short-horizon timer (MIRAGE). These are two different claims and
  only the first is supported.
